audit_findings.title: Equity-method stakes may be counted in both OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $60 million of 2025 equity income, equal to 18.4% of the $326.6 million anchor; $674 million stake bridge; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity income enters historical OE while the investments' carrying value is separately added through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the equity method of accounting, Alliant Energy and WPL initially record the investment at cost, and adjust the carrying amount of the investment to recognize their respective share of the earnings or losses of the investee.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that $60 million of equity-method income was recognized in 2025 and that the investments had a $674 million carrying value. The supplied record does not demonstrate whether that income and its tax effects were removed from OE. If retained, recurring investee earnings are capitalized and the underlying investments are then added again, a scale capable of materially lowering the intrinsic-value estimates if corrected.
audit_findings.action: Trace every OE year to the equity-income accounts and related taxes and distributions; remove all stake-derived economics from OE, retain the $674 million only in the bridge, and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Noncash AFUDC may remain in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $89 million in 2025, equal to 27.3% of the $326.6 million anchor; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: AFUDC credits increase net income and therefore OE despite representing capitalized, noncurrent construction financing returns rather than distributable cash.
audit_findings.evidence: AFUDC represents costs to finance construction additions, including a return on equity component and cost of debt component as required by regulatory accounting.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that 2025 income included $89 million of AFUDC, comprising $63 million of equity AFUDC and $26 million of debt AFUDC. Whether the OE calculation removed those credits is unresolved. Because the annual amount is more than one-quarter of the selected anchor, leaving similar credits in the historical series could materially overstate normalized OE and its terminal capitalization.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to net income and AFUDC by equity and debt component; remove AFUDC credits without also deducting the same noncash capitalized financing amounts through capex, then recompute the trend anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The fixed share ceiling must cover the full future equity-financing requirement
audit_findings.magnitude: 35.417789 million shares between the 259.284699 million current shares and the 294.702488 million ceiling; 25.581305 million outstanding forward shares leave 9.836484 million shares of headroom; $2.4 billion financing plan
audit_findings.mechanism: Future issuances affect the fully diluted share denominator, while their proceeds finance assets supporting projected OE and may also affect the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Alliant Energy currently expects to issue up to $2.4 billion of common stock in aggregate from 2026 through 2029 through the distribution agreement that was executed in May 2025, its Shareholder Direct Plan (up to $25 million in common stock annually) and additional future equity offerings.
audit_findings.explanation: The ceiling already allows 13.7% dilution from the June 2026 outstanding count, but outstanding forward agreements consume most of that allowance. The remaining headroom must also accommodate the rest of the $2.4 billion plan, direct-plan issuance, awards, convertible excess-value settlement and later grants. The record does not establish issuance prices or the exact proceeds treatment, so it cannot establish whether the ceiling is materially too low or whether counted proceeds and operating benefits are omitted or duplicated.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a share-and-proceeds reconciliation from 259.284699 million shares through 2029 using contracted forward terms and issuance-price sensitivities, including all plans, awards and convertibles; verify proceeds against funded capex and the bridge, then rerun per-share values.

audit_findings.title: Tax-credit economics may be finite rather than terminal
audit_findings.magnitude: $250 million of 2025 production and investment tax-credit benefits, equal to 76.5% of the $326.6 million anchor; $285 million of 2025 transfer proceeds and $112 million of regulatory deferrals, not additive
audit_findings.mechanism: Tax benefits and transfer proceeds affect OE, projected growth and the terminal numerator, while regulatory sharing determines how much belongs to common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: The most significant provisions of the new legislation for Alliant Energy, IPL, and WPL relate to the accelerated phase out of clean energy tax credits for eligible wind and solar projects for which construction begins more than 12 months after the enactment date or for projects placed in service after 2027, and restricted access to clean energy tax credits for projects that begin construction after 2025 and receive impermissible amounts of construction support from entities with ties to certain foreign countries, including China.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates substantial recent tax-credit economics and statutory restrictions or phase-outs for affected future projects. It also shows that significant credits are passed to customers or deferred through regulatory accounting. The unresolved issue is whether finite, project-dependent, customer-shared or reinvestment-dependent benefits were embedded in normalized OE and perpetuated. Given their scale relative to the anchor, improper terminal treatment could materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Build a project-by-project credit schedule showing expiration, eligibility, transfer pricing, customer sharing, regulatory deferrals and required capital spending; exclude nonpersistent benefits from terminal OE and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Customer-funded removal obligations may escape the OE capex deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $366 million regulatory liability at 2025-12-31 and $340 million at 2026-06-30; net OE burden unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Removal cash payments are investing outflows outside the usual construction-and-acquisition caption and must enter OE or be recognized through a net bridge liability, after customer funding.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash payments related to cost of removal obligations are included in “Other” in cash flows used for investing activities.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates both the obligation balance and that removal payments are classified within other investing cash flows. It does not establish that the OE pipeline omitted those payments, nor how much of the payments is economically covered by amounts already collected from customers. The gross liability cannot be deducted automatically, but an uncaptured net recurring cash burden could overstate OE; the record cannot establish its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Roll forward the liability using customer collections, cash removal payments and other adjustments for each OE year; identify the unfunded common-equity portion, include it once in OE or the bridge, and rerun if nonzero.

audit_findings.title: ARO costs are deferred from earnings pending regulatory recovery
audit_findings.magnitude: Gross $704 million ARO and $455 million ARO regulatory asset at 2025-12-31; regulatory asset increased to $483 million at 2026-06-30; net common-equity burden unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: ARO settlements can reduce OE or require a bridge deduction when not recovered, while regulatory assets and rates can reimburse costs over time.
audit_findings.evidence: Accretion and depreciation expenses related to AROs for IPL’s and WPL’s regulated operations are recorded to regulatory assets on the balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a large legal obligation and that regulated accretion and depreciation are deferred rather than charged immediately to earnings. It also provides substantial evidence of expected regulatory recovery, so the $704 million gross liability is not a demonstrated common-equity deduction. Recovery timing, disallowance risk and nonregulated or steam-related exposure remain unresolved, preventing the record from establishing a material net burden.
audit_findings.action: Roll forward ARO liabilities, settlements, associated plant and regulatory assets by asset and jurisdiction; document approved recovery amounts and timing, isolate unrecoverable portions, and rerun OE and the bridge for the discounted net common-equity burden only.
